history.rationale: Lys119 forms the Schiff-base (internal aldimine) with the PLP cofactor in the CBS catalytic core (GGSVKD motif, verified K at 119); removing the ε-amino group abolishes catalysis while the fold is largely retained.
Charge reversal at the PLP Schiff-base lysine should eliminate cofactor anchoring and catalysis even more decisively than Ala, with some added risk of local destabilization.
G307 (verified Gly) lies in a tightly packed catalytic-domain loop; G307S is the archetypal severe, pyridoxine-nonresponsive homocystinuria allele with essentially null activity.
Thr191 (verified) sits in the PLP/substrate-binding region; T191M is a well-known severe misfolding/loss-of-function homocystinuria variant.
Thr257 (verified) is in the conserved 'VASVGTGGT' catalytic loop near the active site; bulky Met substitution is a documented severe pathogenic change.
Arg336 (verified) forms buried salt-bridge/H-bond networks in the catalytic core; loss to Cys is a recurrent pathogenic, activity-abolishing substitution.
Gly139 (verified) is in a conserved turn preceding the TSGNTG PLP-binding motif; introducing a large charged Arg should sterically disrupt the active-site scaffold.
Gly305 (verified) is a buried, conformationally constrained glycine adjacent to the G307 loop; Arg insertion should collapse local packing and kill activity.
Arg369 (verified) is a conserved buried arginine in the catalytic domain whose loss is reported in severe homocystinuria; Cys removes its stabilizing interactions.
Ile278 (verified) is the most common homocystinuria allele, destabilizing the catalytic core; ranked lower because I278T retains partial, chaperone/B6-rescuable activity.
